newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr seen recovering in Asia after overnight fall.
newsitem.headline: Dlr seen recovering in Asia after overnight fall.

text.p: The dollar is likely to stay solid against the yen in Asia on Friday due to possible purchases by Japanese securities houses after its fall overnight, with a recovery to 127 yen seen possible, dealers said.
"The dollar could be well-bid at 126.20 yen and may recover to around 127 yen," said a trust bank dealer.
He said yen sales by securities houses related to fresh samurai bond issues could support the dollar against the yen.
But a further recovery above 127 yen is seen difficult due to selling pressure by Japanese exporters and options-related profit-taking near 127.50 yen, and fears of BOJ intervention.
The dollar fell in New York partly due to unconfirmed rumours of looming Bank of Japan intervention.

Dealers here said they were uncertain about possible BOJ intervention. The trust bank dealer said the dollar's overnight fall was mainly due to profit-taking after it was able to break through technical resistance of 127.30 yen.

The dollar rallied to a 56-month peak of 127.47 yen in Tokyo on Thursday. Dealers said they were focusing on the outcome of the British election, with a large victory by the opposition Labour Party seen spurring pound buying against the mark and the yen, which could support the dollar.
The British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) said its election exit poll showed Labour support running at 47 percent and the ruling Conservatives 29 percent.
ITN said their exit poll suggested a Labour majority of 159 seats in the 659-seat parliament.

"A large victory by the Labour Party could raise expectations of an early UK interest rate rise, which may prompt some sterling buying against the mark and that would indirectly support the dollar against the mark," said a Japanese city bank dealer. The market is also waiting for the release of U.S. April unemployment data due out at 1230 GMT.
